key_insight: Decision models can match generative LLM accuracy at much lower cost while reducing—but not eliminating—unsupported legal citations when correct authority is missing.
engineering_relevance: Use decision-model agreement to gate generative answers, and evaluate wrong citations alongside accuracy when building legal verification systems.
method: Replace the correct holding in 1,670 of 5,314 CaseHOLD items to test abstention.
Compare four probability-output decision models with six generative LLMs.
Test agreement-based gating and label-free probability distillation into Qwen3-8B.
evidence_signal: A decision model achieved 88.1% standard CaseHOLD accuracy versus the best generative LLM’s 88.2% at 1/55 of its cost; agreement gating halved that LLM’s wrong citations.
watch_item: Abstention remains imperfect: the most cautious decision model selected an incorrect option on 30% of missing-authority items, and broader legal settings need validation.
paper_title: Commit or Abstain? System One Decision Models, LLMs, and Missing Legal Authority
